channel.title: The Wall Street Journal - CIO Journal
channel.description: Technology leadership and enterprise technology news from CIO Journal

item.title: Tech Outages Are Inevitable. Business Chaos Doesn’t Have to Be.
item.description:
Belle Lin's Morning Download argues that after a string of disruptions that began late last week as more than 450 million Microsoft 365 users lost email, tech leaders should accept that outages are inevitable and focus on resilience, including rehearsing worst-case scenarios and building an undo button for changes. Executives Lin interviewed stressed settling decision rights before a crisis, with TIAA's Sastry Durvasula warning that "Organizations that have to figure this out mid-incident lose hours they don't have," while Netskope's Mike Anderson favored rolling out updates to a small group of employees first. The newsletter also reports that National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving, to be succeeded by Defense Department CIO Kirsten Davies, as the White House draws criticism over its handling of the recent outages.


Sources:

  • Tech Outages Are Inevitable. Business Chaos Doesn’t Have to Be. - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Belle Lin

item.title: Anthropic Pushes the Reset Button for AI
item.description:
The Morning Download argues that Anthropic's record IPO brings some clarity to an AI boom long dogged by doubts over whether revenue and enterprise returns can justify historic capital spending, pointing to the $900.9 billion in compute commitments disclosed in the company's filing, though Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives noted that "The debate from here is margin against growth." Other demand signals come from Alibaba, whose fiscal second-quarter profit surged as its AI profitability improved, and Walmart, whose global e-commerce sales grew 17% after years of technology investment. The newsletter also covers tech founders rallying behind Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia and AI talk at the CMO Council Summit, where Visa CMO Frank Cooper III said marketers are now "entering B to AI."


Sources:

  • Anthropic Pushes the Reset Button for AI - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Nvidia Results Show AI Demand Remains Robust
item.description:
The Morning Download argues that Nvidia's first investor call under interim chief executive Colette Kress showed AI demand is not only robust but accelerating nearly four years after ChatGPT's debut, and that the call settled the market's acceptance of Kress, marking what felt like the real end of former CEO Jensen Huang's era. The newsletter also takes up the past week's run of outages, from a global Microsoft disruption to an FAA ground stop and a National Security Agency network failure, which the companies blame on botched upgrades rather than hackers; security experts largely attribute this year's record volume of upgrades in North America to AI, and Microsoft's update last month fixed about 1,400 flaws versus about 170 a year earlier. Its advice is that leaders explain quickly before fear fills the gap, pointing to the federal response to Friday's ground stop, which former DHS official Brian Harrell called "bumbling" and "insufficient".


Sources:

  • Nvidia Results Show AI Demand Remains Robust - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Thomson Reuters Chief Forges Path With AI, Unique Content
item.description:
Thomson Reuters CEO Steve Hasker told Rosenbush that he began rebuilding the company around AI in 2020, well before ChatGPT, and argues that proprietary, curated content matters more than even chips or energy in making AI output accurate, though the stock has lagged the S&P 500 since August 2025. Rosenbush writes that big-company CEOs sticking with long-term AI investments, along with startups such as Genesis AI that are still raising money, are providing "ballast" amid volatile valuations and policy. The newsletter also previews the Nvidia earnings report due that day and notes WSJ reporting that Nvidia's independent directors have drawn almost $188 million in board compensation over 20 years.


Sources:

  • Thomson Reuters Chief Forges Path With AI, Unique Content - wsj.com

item.title: Genesis AI, a Robotics Startup, Raises $500 Million
item.description:
Paris-based Genesis AI, a robotics startup only about two years old, has raised $500 million in a Series A round led jointly by Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures and Eclipse that values it at $3.5 billion, with backers including Nvidia's and AMD's venture arms and individuals such as former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. The company builds its entire technology stack for a general-purpose robot called Eno, and CEO Zhou Xian said the money will expand data collection and large-scale training, while the round will also grow its team of researchers and engineers. Xian, 32, predicted a robotics model that "just works out of the box" sometime next year, and Khosla Ventures founder Vinod Khosla pointed to the team's "scrappiness and speed" as what caught his attention.


Sources:

  • Genesis AI, a Robotics Startup, Raises $500 Million - wsj.com

item.title: Nvidia CEO Ouster Reverberates Globally
item.description:
The Morning Download argues that Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO could rank among the most consequential corporate shake-ups ever, with effects rippling through chipmakers, venture-backed startups and geopolitics, though it says the move does not mean the end of Nvidia or of global AI adoption. According to records the Journal reviewed, Megaspeed, a company tied to Alice Huang, whom the newsletter identifies as Huang's onetime mistress, set up close to $12 billion in shipments of top Nvidia chips to Chinese buyers, though they don't show how many arrived and Megaspeed says it follows U.S. export controls. Startups expect Nvidia, now led by interim CEO Colette Kress, to pull back further from its role as an "open checkbook" for AI, a shift UBS estimates could remove $50 billion or more from the market, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged the board to pick an outsider as CEO.


Sources:

  • Nvidia CEO Ouster Reverberates Globally - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Nvidia Needs Three CEOs in One
item.description:
In the Morning Download, Steven Rosenbush and former Apple, Microsoft and Google executive Sophia Velastegui contrast Apple's carefully signaled handoff from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook with Nvidia's abrupt, unplanned search after Jensen Huang's exit. "Nvidia needs three leaders in one," Velastegui said: a technologist engineers will follow, a trusted steward of the CUDA platform, and a statesperson Washington and Taipei will take calls from. She names AMD's Lisa Su, Google's Amin Vahdat and insider Ian Buck as possibilities and argues the next CEO must sell entire AI factories to governments, not just chips to cloud companies.


Sources:

  • Nvidia Needs Three CEOs in One - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Nvidia Board Must Craft Epic Job Description for New CEO
item.description:
In the Morning Download, Steven Rosenbush argues that Nvidia's board faces a daunting search after Jensen Huang resigned following two extramarital affairs, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy, since the company needs a successor with Jobs-level instincts for innovation and sales who can also instill greater calm and discipline and take "a less-imperial approach to leadership." Longtime CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO, and Nvidia stock dropped more than 7% before the opening bell while other chip stocks slipped far less. The newsletter also notes that Nvidia quit reporting its Singapore revenue separately soon after cutting off Megaspeed, the Singapore firm tied to the espionage scandal, and has declined to say whether the two moves were connected.


Sources:

  • Nvidia Board Must Craft Epic Job Description for New CEO - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: AI Startup LangChain More Than Doubles Its Valuation to $3 Billion
item.description:
LangChain, whose software helps developers build AI apps and agents, raised $300 million in a round led by Alphabet's CapitalG that values it at $3 billion, more than twice its valuation from October of last year, Belle Lin reports. The money will go toward expanding LangSmith, the startup's platform for monitoring, evaluating and deploying agents, as many enterprises hold back on agents until governance is in place; "The agent's behavior is the hard part to control," said co-founder and CEO Harrison Chase. CapitalG partner Mo Jomaa called the field "an insanely competitive market" in which big players try to lock customers into their own ecosystems, and the three-year-old company plans to grow from 435 full-time staff to 850 by the end of next year.


Sources:

  • AI Startup LangChain More Than Doubles Its Valuation to $3 Billion - wsj.com

item.title: AI Is Testing the Limits of Corporate Governance
item.description:
Drawing on remarks at the WSJ Leadership Institute's board summit in Palm Beach, Steven Rosenbush writes that directors regard AI as here to stay and want governance to keep pace, with SLB and Adidas board member Jing Ulrich saying "Technology changes faster than governance" and ExCo Group's Shellye Archambeau noting that the talk has shifted from cutting heads to driving strategy. GM and Procter & Gamble director Joe Jimenez asked how the next generation of leaders will develop if AI eliminates or radically reshapes entry-level jobs. The newsletter also notes that CoreWeave beat revenue expectations and raised its guidance, and that Wachtell Lipton will lead an independent probe into whether Nvidia was targeted by foreign espionage.


Sources:

  • AI Is Testing the Limits of Corporate Governance - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Why Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Is Unique
item.description:
Steven Rosenbush writes that Nvidia's board may test whether anyone is truly irreplaceable, crediting Jensen Huang's founder vision for turning an early bet on videogame graphics chips into a $4.5 trillion AI powerhouse while warning that Huang's misstep has put the company "in a uniquely precarious position." Some attendees at the WSJ Leadership Institute's board summit questioned whether Nvidia's directors moved too quickly to protect Huang over his relationship with a Singapore-based data center executive whom U.S. officials believe fed intelligence to China, and the newsletter notes the chip maker has no chairman, no succession plan and, as of last spring, three of its 10 independent directors in their seats for 25 years or more. It also covers President Trump's defense of Huang ("I really believe him") and several tech leaders' plans to push ahead with AI whatever happens to regulation after the election.


Sources:

  • Why Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Is Unique - wsj.com
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Enterprises Say AI Regulation Won’t Stop Corporate Innovation
item.description:
Corporate tech leaders who spoke with the WSJ Leadership Institute say they will press ahead with AI whatever rules emerge under Democratic control of Congress and state offices, citing their own internal guardrails and the view that today's models already do what they need. Sutherland CIO Doug Gilbert said everyday work has an "extremely low" need for the most powerful frontier models, and Intuit CTO Alex Balazs said his company is investing heavily in its AI harness, the software layer that runs models and lets businesses mix providers. Many of the executives expect AI policy to stay at the state level for now, a patchwork that Appian CEO Matt Calkins warned could be "irregular across the nation".


Sources:

  • Enterprises Say AI Regulation Won’t Stop Corporate Innovation - wsj.com

item.title: Ready to Start Your Next Car Lease With an AI Chatbot? BMW Wants to Help.
item.description:
This Morning Download leads with BMW's new U.S. ChatGPT app, which lets shoppers check local inventory, configure a vehicle, build a lease financing package and book a test drive, though the lease itself must still be completed at a dealer. BMW of North America marketing vice president Leigh Moynihan called the app "a must do" as more customers research cars with chatbots, and North America chief customer officer Andreas Walter said the team tested heavily to make sure "there's no hallucination going on" in financial answers. The newsletter also covers the Nvidia board's probe of reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a suspected Chinese spy, and a jobs report showing a 70,000-job gain in professional and business services.


Sources:

  • Ready to Start Your Next Car Lease With an AI Chatbot? BMW Wants to Help. - wsj.com
